_what: The shapes and words for setting up the ways an account signs in besides its passkeys, when the person adds them: backup codes (how many, how grouped, from which characters) and an authenticator app (how long a setup waits for its first right code, how many tries a setup gets). Read by read-data/verify-every-port-sign-in-authenticator-setup.mjs. Adding or changing a way in asks for a recent sign-in (fresh_minutes), so a browser left signed in cannot quietly add a way in for someone else. The authenticator app's label shown in the app is not here: it is named by the owner that wires the setup. Ported from the earlier code base's src/sign-in-methods.json and src/sign-in-methods.mjs (b6ae0ebf815f). Sign-in tries, the email index and the storage of codes are not here.

words.sign_in_again: For your safety, sign in again first. Opening sign-in…
words.backup_made: Keep these somewhere safe, away from this device. Each works once.
words.backup_reveal: Your {count} backup codes. Copy them now: they are shown only this once.
words.authenticator_on: Your authenticator app is on. It shows a new code for the service every 30 seconds.
words.authenticator_wrong: That code is not right. Type the newest code your authenticator app shows for the service.
words.authenticator_setup_ended: This setup ended. Open it again from Account & security.
words.authenticator_removed: Your authenticator app is removed. Its codes no longer sign in.
words.authenticator_too_many: Too many tries. Wait {minutes} minutes, then try again.
